title: Let AI models trade crypto with $10k each
summary: Nof1's Alpha Arena gave six AI models $10,000 each to trade crypto on Hyperliquid with no human help; GNcrypto reports only Qwen 3 Max and DeepSeek finished in profit.
model: Qwen 3 Max, DeepSeek, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok, GPT-5
agent_role: Each model decided and executed its own trades on live markets; organizers set the prompts and rules and did not intervene during the season.
outcome: Qwen 3 Max finished first at $12,231 and DeepSeek second at $10,489; the other four models ended with large losses
what_they_did: Nof1.ai ran Alpha Arena Season 1 from October 18 to November 3, 2025. Six models each got $10,000: Qwen 3 Max, DeepSeek v3.1, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Grok 4. They traded a type of crypto contract with no end date on the Hyperliquid exchange, with no human help. The organizers set the instructions and rules, and the models chose and placed their own trades.
how_it_went: GNcrypto reports Qwen 3 Max won with about 22% returns, finishing at $12,231. DeepSeek was the only other model to make a profit, ending at $10,489. GPT-5 did worst, ending with around $3,733.
worth_knowing: Nof1 founder Jay Azhang said the models only got streams of numbers over time, which these models don't handle well, plus few assets and limited actions. He also saw the same biases persist across many rewrites of the instructions.
prompt: Act as a paper-trading agent for [asset list] using [data source]. Each [interval], review recent price data, decide whether to open, close or hold a position within a simulated balance of [starting amount], and log each decision with a short rationale. Do not place real trades or move any money. At the end of [test period], summarize performance, drawdowns and any recurring biases in your decisions. Show me your trading rules and logging format first and wait for my approval before starting.
